newsitem.title: GERMANY: Blair calls for change in Europe's course - report.
newsitem.headline: Blair calls for change in Europe's course - report.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair called for fundamental change in the course of European politics in a front-page commentary in Germany's mass-circulation Bild newspaper.

Blair, ahead of an official visit on Friday to Bonn, said in the article that he expected to have good relations with Chancellor Helmut Kohl and to improve the ties with Germany, which he said was Britain's largest trading partner.

"Above all, I am going to recommend a new course for Europe," Blair said in the commentary in German. "All too often the people of Europe feel very far away from what the top politicians say and do. That must change."
"We must worry about the true interests of the public: jobs, crime, environment, security," Blair said.

Blair said his meeting with Kohl would be his first journey to meet with a foreign leader and that he wanted relations with Germany, which were strained under former Prime Minister John Major, to improve.
"I want the relationship between our two countries to clearly improve, and I believe we will succeed," Blair said.
